Figure output

Source: R/figure.R
pub_figure.Rd

Marks a plot or image files as a figure and sets its caption, size and other metadata.

Usage

pub_figure(
  x,
  caption = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  out_width = NULL,
  ...,
  render = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A ggplot, a recorded plot (grDevices::recordPlot()) or the paths of existing image files of one figure (see Details). A rendered figure (render = TRUE) can be passed again to set its metadata.

caption

character(1) caption (figures are numbered) or NULL.

width, height

Size of the plot in inches (default 8 x 6).

out_width

Width in the document relative to the text width, e.g. "90%" (default).

...

Further metadata, e.g. title, id (to refer to the figure as @fig:<id> in texts, see pub_text()), landscape or locked (see pub_meta()).

render

TRUE: draw a ggplot or recorded plot now, as a png image (see Details, "Rendered figures"); must be named.

Value

x with metadata; with render = TRUE the png image (class pub_png) of the plot, with the same metadata.

Details

When do you need it?

Plots in a document (pub_doc()) are figures even without pub_figure(); use it only to set a caption or a size. Image files, however, always need it, as otherwise their paths would be read as text:

Inputpub_figure()
ggplotoptional
recorded base plot (grDevices::recordPlot())optional
image files (png, jpg, svg, pdf)required

One figure in several formats

You can pass several image files of the same plot, e.g. a png and a pdf. Each output format then picks the file that suits it best:

  • HTML and DOCX show the png (or jpg), as they can't show pdf images;

  • a PDF report made with LaTeX can use the vector graphic if you ask for it with figure = list(device = "pdf") (see pub_html() and pub_report_spec()).

Always provide at least a png or jpg.

Rendered figures

With render = TRUE the plot is drawn where the step runs and the step returns the png image (200 dpi, class pub_png) instead of the plot. Use it:

  • in steps that run in other R processes (workers) and for pipelines saved with saveRDS(): a ggplot holds environments, so a copy of it differs from the original, and the document renders it again even though nothing changed. The image has no environments and survives copying unchanged, so the document uses it as it is;

  • for recorded plots, which can't be replayed in another R session.

Note that once rendered, a figure can't be changed in later steps, so the rendering step should be the last that touches it. In addition, even if a report spec has figure = list(device = "pdf") it still shows the png.

A rendered figure takes caption, id etc. like any other; changing them later (also with pub_set_meta()) only affects the metadata, not the image. width and height are the exception: they are the size the plot was rendered at, so pub_figure() refuses them (use out_width to scale the figure in the document). pub_set_meta() accepts them, but then they no longer match the pixels.

See also

pub_meta(), pub_type()

Examples

# A recorded base plot is a figure already; pub_figure() adds a caption and size
grDevices::pdf(NULL)
grDevices::dev.control("enable")
plot(1:10)
p <- grDevices::recordPlot()
grDevices::dev.off()
#> agg_record_1d6f40adae82 
#>                       2 
pub_type(p)
#> [1] "figure"

fig <- pub_figure(p, caption = "Ten points", width = 5, height = 4, id = "points")
pub_type(fig)
#> [1] "figure"
pub_meta(fig)
#> $caption
#> [1] "Ten points"
#> 
#> $width
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $height
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $id
#> [1] "points"
#> 

# The same holds for a ggplot
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
    gg <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) +
        ggplot2::geom_point()
    print(pub_type(gg))
    pub_meta(pub_figure(gg, caption = "Weight and mileage"))
}
#> [1] "figure"
#> $caption
#> [1] "Weight and mileage"
#> 

# Image files must be marked, otherwise their paths are text
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
ragg::agg_png(file)
plot(1:10)
grDevices::dev.off()
#> agg_record_1d6f40adae82 
#>                       2 
pub_type(file)
#> [1] "text"
pub_type(pub_figure(file, caption = "Ten points from a file"))
#> [1] "figure"

# One figure in several formats: a renderer picks the best file
files <- file.path(tempdir(), c("points.png", "points.pdf"))
ragg::agg_png(files[1])
plot(1:10)
grDevices::dev.off()
#> agg_record_1d6f40adae82 
#>                       2 
grDevices::pdf(files[2])
plot(1:10)
grDevices::dev.off()
#> agg_record_1d6f40adae82 
#>                       2 
fig <- pub_figure(files, caption = "Ten points as png and pdf")
html <- pub_html(pub_doc(fig))  # HTML picks the png
grepl("data:image/png", html)
#> [1] TRUE

# Render the figure in the step: the result is a png image with the metadata
png <- pub_figure(p, caption = "Ten points", width = 4, height = 3, render = TRUE)
png
#> <pubflow figure> PNG 800 x 600 px (4 x 3 in, 200 dpi), 18 KB
#> Caption: Ten points
pub_type(png)
#> [1] "figure"
identical(png, unserialize(serialize(png, NULL)))
#> [1] TRUE
